setting: A fictional discussion with a project manager who is confident in a team decision.

presentation.situation: {{name}}, your project manager, decided to {{decision}}. You think that is a mistake, because {{evidence}}. Challenge it without damaging the relationship, and offer an alternative: {{alternative}}.
presentation.opening: The team has agreed to {{decision}}, so I don't see a reason to reopen this.

brief.you_are: You disagree with your project manager, and you want to keep a good working relationship.
brief.situation: {{name}}, your project manager, decided to {{decision}}. You think that is a mistake, because {{evidence}}. Challenge it without damaging the relationship, and offer an alternative: {{alternative}}.
brief.task: Acknowledge common ground, explain your concern with evidence, and offer an alternative.
brief.done_looks_like: {{name}} has heard your concern and evidence, has an alternative to consider, and still respects you.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You disagree with your project manager, and you want to keep a good working relationship.
goals: Acknowledge common ground, explain your concern with evidence, and offer an alternative.

card.want: To keep the project moving, and not to reopen every decision.
card.hidden_need: Is under pressure to show progress, and fears looking indecisive.
card.attitude: Confident, a little impatient, and persuaded only by evidence.
card.speech: Fluent, natural professional English. Direct, and free of corporate slogans.

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: {{name}} made the decision under pressure from senior management to show progress.

objectives.evidence: The learner acknowledges common ground or the manager's goal.
alternatives: I agree we need to move fast.

objectives.evidence: The learner explains the concern, using evidence.
alternatives: My concern is that we saw this fail last time, because...

objectives.evidence: The learner proposes a practical alternative.
alternatives: An alternative would be to pilot it with one team first.

beats.orient: You disagree with me, but you still want to work together. Start by saying what you agree with. You can say: I agree that.

opportunity: That is an opinion. What makes you say that?
beats.orient: Now tell me your concern, and use the evidence in your brief. Start with: My concern is.
fallback: That is an opinion. What makes you say that?

opportunity: So what would you do instead?
beats.orient: Now give me an alternative. Start with: An alternative would be.
fallback: So what would you do instead?

closing_line: All right, I hear you. Let's look at that properly. Thanks for raising it directly.

o1.good: Starting with what you share lowers defences.
o1.micro_lesson: Say: I agree that, or: We both want.
o1.model: I agree we need to move fast, and I want this to succeed.

o2.good: Evidence, not opinion, and about the plan, not the person.
o2.micro_lesson: Say: My concern is, then: because.
o2.model: My concern is the risk, because of what happened in the last release.

o3.good: Bringing a solution as well as a problem.
common_mistakes: Criticizing, with nothing to offer instead
o3.model: An alternative would be to pilot it with one team first.

variants.name: Karen
variants.decision: move every customer to the new system in one weekend
variants.evidence: last year's one-weekend move caused two days of outages

variants.name: Faisal
variants.decision: cut the testing phase in half to meet the date
variants.evidence: most serious defects last quarter were found in the second half of testing
variants.alternative: keeping full testing for the payment features only
